image_description: A vintage black Smith-Corona typewriter sitting on a wooden surface. The image focuses on the keyboard and carriage area. The 'space bar' is the long, horizontal black lever located at the bottom center of the keybed, below the round letter keys.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated rectangular key spanning the full width of the bottom keyboard row.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The space bar on this typewriter does not span the *full* width of the keyboard; it is centrally located but leaves significant gaps on the left and right sides before the frame/other mechanisms. It is elongated, but the 'full width' descriptor from the modern keyboard taxonomy is inaccurate here.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Length is dramatically greater than any other key, roughly ten times the width of a standard letter key.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The space bar is significantly longer than the round circular keys above it, satisfying the relative proportion requirement.

The material appears to be painted metal or hard rubber typical of vintage typewriters, exhibiting a slight sheen/gloss rather than the matte plastic finish described in the modern taxonomy.
